props.eyebrow: Event music at a Downtown Denver hotel
props.title: Grand Hyatt Denver
props.lede: Grand Hyatt Denver is on Welton Street in the middle of downtown, and its Pinnacle Club, on the 38th floor, has some of the best views of the Rockies in the city.

headingText.html: Downstairs, the Colorado and Aspen ballrooms handle the bigger dinners, conference receptions and weddings.

props.title: Live music in each Grand Hyatt Denver event space
props.lede: Here’s the act we’d pick for each space. Press play to hear it over the photo.

spaces.name: Pinnacle Club
spaces.facts: The Pinnacle Club is on the 38th floor, about 4,200 sq ft with views of the mountains and the city. It used to be the Petroleum Club, and the hotel uses it for weddings and receptions of up to about 350.
spaces.why: Upright bass and guitar, at a volume nobody has to raise their voice over.
spaces.alt: The Pinnacle Club set with cocktail tables, with the mountains through tall windows.

spaces.name: Colorado Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Colorado Ballroom is about 8,400 sq ft with 18-foot ceilings, for banquets of up to 640 and receptions of up to 1,000. It divides into two halves, with a foyer outside.
spaces.why: A six-piece band playing 90s and 2000s R&B and hip-hop, for when you want everyone dancing.
spaces.alt: The Colorado Ballroom set for a gala dinner, with screens either side of a lit stage.

spaces.name: Aspen Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Aspen Ballroom is about 5,900 sq ft, for banquets of up to 450 and receptions of up to 700.
spaces.why: Rock covers everyone knows, with a powerhouse singer out front.
spaces.alt: The Aspen Ballroom set with round tables and red flowers under crystal chandeliers.

spaces.name: Maroon Peak
spaces.facts: Maroon Peak is about 960 sq ft, for dinners of up to 70.
spaces.why: A solo violin to a full string quartet, from the ceremony through dinner.

props.title: Planning music at Grand Hyatt Denver

rows.text: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space.
The Pinnacle Club is on the 38th floor, so we plan the elevator and load-in with the hotel’s events team ahead of time.
The hotel caters events in-house, and its wedding packages include the catering.
There’s self-parking and valet at the hotel.

props.html: Questions to ask the Grand Hyatt Denver events team

items.html: Which spaces have an end time for amplified music, and when is it?
Does the hotel’s AV team need to connect or run the band’s sound, and is there a fee for that?
Where do vendors load in, and when can the band set up?
Is there power near where the band will play?
What wording do you need on the certificate of insurance?

props.html: Forward this list to the events team, or send us the answers and we’ll plan around them.
Questions about music at Grand Hyatt Denver

items.q: Can we bring our own band to an event at Grand Hyatt Denver?
items.a: Hotels like Grand Hyatt Denver generally let you book your own entertainment, within their rules on insurance, load-in and sound. Your event manager can confirm them for your date, and we send a certificate of insurance with every booking.

items.q: Does the band need the hotel’s AV team?
items.a: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space. The hotel’s AV team can add anything beyond that, and we’ll work out the details with your event manager.

items.q: Can one act play the ceremony, the cocktail hour and the reception?
items.a: Yes. The same act can move with you through the day, and one booking covers all of it.

items.q: How much does live music add to an event at Grand Hyatt Denver?
items.a: It depends on the size of the act and how much of the day it covers. Our pricing page has what live music costs in the Colorado market, and we’ll send a quote for your date.
